title: MOFA solemnly refutes false claims regarding ROC (Taiwan) in China-Gabon joint statement
text:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) strongly protests false claims made in a joint statement issued after a meeting between Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema on November 6. In the statement, Gabon reaffirmed its adherence to the “one China principle,” China’s misrepresentation of United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758, and other falsehoods. MOFA solemnly denounces the Chinese government’s continued use of bilateral talks to cajole other countries into making untrue statements that degrade Taiwan’s sovereignty.

MOFA reiterates the following: The ROC (Taiwan) is a sovereign, independent country; neither it nor the People’s Republic of China (PRC) is subordinate to the other; the PRC has never governed Taiwan; and only the democratically elected government of Taiwan has the right to represent the Taiwanese people in international settings, including within the UN system. China and its allies have no say in these matters. Taiwan will not tolerate China’s repeated attempts to unilaterally alter the status quo by spreading disinformation and authoritarian propaganda under the guise of so-called bilateral statements.

In its efforts to undermine the international order, China has long aggressively sought to include references to the so-called “one China principle” in bilateral agreements with other countries. MOFA reiterates that no statement or document can change the fact that neither side of the Taiwan Strait is subordinate to the other. It strongly advises the Gabonese government to maintain objectivity and neutrality, not to blindly follow China’s deliberate political manipulation, and to pay heed to the potential threat that China’s actions pose to regional peace. （E）
